source.title: Park the local heap while a thread waits inside the replay runtime

nodes.body:
### Review of `ce56ab523ee5`

🟡 **Merge risk: moderate** — 1 should-fix finding open.

🔴 **Prod risk: 1** — finding in production code worth acting on.

🟠 **Should fix**: 1

#### Prod risk (1)

- `src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp`
  - 🟠 **Should fix** Thread::Wait builds two new ABI thunks on every wait in Windows replay, and moving the wrap into Wait makes this run far more often — [L522](https://github.com/replayio/backend/blob/ce56ab523ee57dd21effb9b776552f0c3923151f/src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp#L522) · _[1]_ <!-- ai-review kind=summary-item file=src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp line=522 fp=685d957694 sev=should-fix -->

**Intent:** ⚠️ Partly matches the description — The PR title and description describe wrapping only the wait for an ordered lock's turn, but the diff wraps every `Thread::Wait`; only the second commit message mentions this.

**What it does:** Adds a replay-only hook, RecordReplaySetWaitWhileParkedCallback, that a target installs to wrap blocking waits. Thread::Wait, when not preparing for a fork and a callback is installed, hands the callback a trampoline that does the raw wait; otherwise it waits as before.

**What to focus on:** Thread::Wait now routes every non-fork block through an optional target callback so V8 can park its local heap and avoid a safepoint deadlock. Review the single behavioral change in Thread::Wait and the callback/ABI plumbing around it.

**Start here**

1. [`src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp`](https://github.com/replayio/backend/blob/ce56ab523ee57dd21effb9b776552f0c3923151f/src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp) — Holds the only behavioral change: the new branch in Thread::Wait, the trampoline and the callback setter.
1. [`src/cpp/linker/Thread.h`](https://github.com/replayio/backend/blob/ce56ab523ee57dd21effb9b776552f0c3923151f/src/cpp/linker/Thread.h) — Declares BlockedWaitFn and the setter, and documents the exactly-once contract and the deadlock rationale.
1. [`src/cpp/api.html`](https://github.com/replayio/backend/blob/ce56ab523ee57dd21effb9b776552f0c3923151f/src/cpp/api.html) — Public contract that targets such as V8 will rely on.

📄 **[Full review detail](https://github.com/replayio/backend/actions/runs/45075099526/artifacts/14774981822)** — download the `ai-code-review-14148-ce56ab523` artifact and open `backend-pr14148-ce56ab523ee5-20261122215957.detail.md` for the walkthrough and the evidence behind each finding. Artifacts expire 90 days after the run.

<details><summary>What the reviewers checked (3)</summary>

- The `Driver.cpp` stub `RecordReplaySetWaitWhileParkedCallback` (`src/cpp/driver/Driver.cpp:792`) has the same signature as the `api.html` declaration and as `SetWaitWhileParkedCallback`'s `BlockedWaitFn` parameter (`src/cpp/linker/Thread.h:385,397`).
- `Thread::Wait` (`src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp:519-520`) still checks `ShouldPrepareForFork` before calling the callback, so the fork path never runs target code. `PerformBlockedWait` calls `WaitRaw` on the same thread, so `WaitRaw`'s `this == Current()` assert (`src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp:529`) holds.
- The target's callback is stored after `ConvertCallbackTargetToDriver` (`src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp:511`), which matches how other linker callback setters convert target callbacks.

</details>

<details><summary>Copy all findings as Markdown</summary>

```markdown
# Review findings: PR #14148 Let the target wrap the wait for an ordered lock's recorded turn

Base `301176326cd0`, head `ce56ab523ee5`

1 finding: 1 should-fix.

### [should-fix] Thread::Wait builds two new ABI thunks on every wait in Windows replay, and moving the wrap into Wait makes this run far more often

`src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp:522` · id `685d957694`

Same defect as the one I reported last time at `OrderedLock.cpp:268`, but the code moved and that made it worse. The conversion is now in `Thread::Wait`, which every block in the runtime goes through, not only the ordered-lock turn. `PerformBlockedWait` is a fixed static function, so its target-ABI form only has to be built once. Doing it once, in `SetWaitWhileParkedCallback` or lazily into a static, removes the per-wait cost. On non-Windows targets `ConvertCallbackDriverToTarget` returns its argument unchanged, so the cost only shows up in Windows replay.

This replaces the summary item previously reported at `src/cpp/recording/OrderedLock.cpp:268`; that code is gone and the per-wait conversion now sits in `Thread::Wait` (`src/cpp/linker/Thread.cpp:522`), which also covers joins (`Thread.cpp:494`) and `WaitForeverForRecordedCall` (`Thread.cpp:559`).

**Impact:** When a Windows recording is replayed with a callback installed, every blocked wait (lock turns, stream chunk loads, condvar waits, joins) assembles and leaks two pieces of executable code and adds a frame-size entry. Memory grows for the whole replay, and the hottest blocking path now pays for code generation on each call.

**Evidence:** `ConvertCallbackDriverToTarget` (`src/cpp/intercept/Intercept.h:252-257`) calls `ConvertCallbackSystemVToFastcall` when `TARGET_WINDOWS && !RECORDING`. `ConvertCallbackSystemVToFastcallRaw` (`src/cpp/intercept/Intercept.cpp:453-460`) calls both `CreateInvoke` and `CreateIntercept`. Each of those assembles new code with `masm.finish()`, and `CreateIntercept` also calls `Binary::SetFrameSize` (`src/cpp/intercept/Intercept.cpp:310-316`); nothing caches the result.

**Suggestion:** In `SetWaitWhileParkedCallback`, convert `&Thread::PerformBlockedWait` once and store it in a static. `Wait()` then passes the stored pointer.
```
